# FDG9061

> DO NOT implement coercion logic in dependency property accessors.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.3.5 Dependency Property Value Coercion.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Not an analyzer candidate of its own: coercion in an accessor of a dependency property is code other than the standard code, which FDG9057 reports; whether that code is coercion is judgment, and the validator does not let a rule list another rule's analyzer diagnostic.

## From the book

Dependency properties have a built-in coercion feature, and it can be used by supplying a coercion callback to the `PropertyMetadata`.

```csharp
public static readonly DependencyProperty TextProperty =
  DependencyProperty.Register(
    "Text",
    typeof(string),
    typeof(TextButton),
      new PropertyMetadata(
        string.Empty,
        (obj, args) => {
          // change notification callback
        },
        (obj, value) => value ?? string.Empty)); // coercion
```
